title: Check yourself: defining and using records

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: `record Booking(LocalDate checkIn, LocalDate checkOut)` has a compact constructor whose only statement is `if (!checkOut().isAfter(checkIn())) throw new IllegalArgumentException();`. What does `new Booking(LocalDate.of(2025, 3, 10), LocalDate.of(2025, 3, 12))` do?

options.text: It returns a booking, since the accessors return the arguments the body was given
options.says: the accessors read the fields, and the fields are assigned only after the compact body ends

options.text: It throws NullPointerException, since the accessors return the fields' default values
options.says: while the compact body runs the fields hold their defaults, null for LocalDate, so checkOut() returns null and isAfter is called on null

options.text: It throws IllegalArgumentException, since the accessors return the fields' default values
options.says: the defaults of LocalDate fields are null, not equal dates, so isAfter is called on null and throws NullPointerException before the check can decide

options.text: It returns a booking, since the accessors are not called until the body has ended
options.says: the body runs the calls where they stand; only the field assignment waits until the body ends

origin.section: The Compact Constructor Runs Before the Fields Are Assigned, So It Checks the Parameters

questions.stem: `record Money(long cents, String currency) implements Serializable` has no compact constructor. A second constructor, `Money(String text)`, parses "12.50 EUR", calls `this(...)`, and then throws if `cents < 0`. A producer with a bug builds `new Money(-500, "EUR")` and sends it serialized; the consumer reads it back with `ObjectInputStream`. What does the consumer get?

options.text: An InvalidObjectException, since reading it back runs the constructor that holds the check
options.says: deserialization calls the canonical constructor and nothing else, and the check is not there

options.text: An InvalidObjectException, since a check placed after this(...) runs whenever the canonical constructor does
options.says: the call goes one way: Money(String) calls the canonical constructor, never the reverse, so the check guards only callers of Money(String)

options.text: A Money of -500 cents, since reading it back calls the canonical constructor, which has no check
options.says: every path to a record, deserialization included, ends in the canonical constructor; a check elsewhere guards one path

options.text: A Money of -500 cents, since reading it back sets a record's fields without calling any constructor
options.says: the outcome is right but the reason is a class's: a record is rebuilt through its canonical constructor

origin.section: A Custom Constructor Must Call the Canonical One First, So Checks Belong in the Canonical One

questions.stem: Given `interface Priced { long cents(); }`, a developer writes `record Item(String sku, long cents) implements Priced {}` with an empty body. What does javac do with it?

options.text: It refuses Item, since java.lang.Record already declares a final method of that name
options.says: the compiler writes the accessor in Item from its component; java.lang.Record has no cents() method to clash with

options.text: It refuses Item, since a generated accessor is too weakly accessible for an interface method
options.says: a generated accessor is public, which is why it can implement an interface method

options.text: It compiles, since java.lang.Record supplies the interface method for Item
options.says: the compiler writes the accessor in Item from its component; java.lang.Record has no cents() method

options.text: It compiles, since a generated accessor supplies the interface method for Item
options.says: the generated accessor has the interface method's name, return type and public access, so it implements it

origin.section: A Record's Body Adds Methods, Static Members and Interfaces, but No Instance Field

questions.stem: To log how old a request is, a developer adds `private final Instant created = Instant.now();` to the body of `record Visit(String page)`. What happens?

options.text: It compiles, and two visits to the same page are equal when created matches too
options.says: a record can't declare an instance field at all; all instance state is a component

options.text: It compiles, and two visits to the same page are equal whatever created holds
options.says: the declaration is refused; a record's only instance fields are those of its components

options.text: It fails to compile, since a record body accepts static fields and no others
options.says: javac reports `field declaration must be static` and suggests a record component instead

options.text: It fails to compile, since Instant.now() can't be called while a record is being constructed
options.says: the refusal is about any instance field in the body, initialised or not; methods can be called during construction, as the compact constructor's own body shows

origin.section: A Record's Body Adds Methods, Static Members and Interfaces, but No Instance Field

questions.stem: Inside `static Map<String, Long> totals(List<Sale> sales, String currency)`, a developer declares `record Row(String region, long cents) { String key() { return region + "/" + currency; } }` maps each sale to a `Row`, and groups the rows by `Row::key`. What does javac do?

options.text: It compiles, since a local record captures the method's variable as a lambda would
options.says: a local record is implicitly static, unlike a lambda or a local class, so it captures nothing

options.text: It refuses Row, since a local record is static and can't read the method's variables
options.says: javac reports `non-static variable currency cannot be referenced from a static context`; pass currency in as a component

options.text: It compiles, since a local record turns the variable into a hidden component
options.says: a record has no state outside its header, which is why it can't capture the variable

options.text: It refuses Row, since a local record can't be declared inside a static method
options.says: local records are allowed in any method body, static or not; the error is the captured variable

origin.section: Nested and Local Records Are Static, So They Can't Reach an Outer Instance or a Local Variable

concepts: A generated accessor whose name and type match an interface method implements it, with no body needed.
A compact constructor's body runs before the fields are assigned, so accessors and other instance methods called there see default values; checks read the parameters.
Deserializing a record calls its canonical constructor and no other, so a check in another constructor doesn't run.
Nested and local records are implicitly static, so they can't read an enclosing instance's fields or a method's local variables; such values become components.
A record's body may declare static fields, static and instance methods and nested types, but no instance field.
